title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap (Q2 2026 playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This doc is the canonical operational playbook for Platform Systems & Services (PSS). It consolidates the systems inventory, runbooks, dashboards and alerting standards, a short retrospective for the last high-severity incident, and a prioritized roadmap for Q2-Q4 2026. The intended audience is on-call engineers, platform maintainers, and platform product owners.

Goals

- Reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for P1 incidents to < 25 minutes.
- Keep platform-wide SLO compliance >= 99.9% (service availability, median request latency).
- Consolidate dashboards to a single Grafana workspace and reduce duplicate alerts by 40% by end of Q3 2026.

Systems inventory (high level)

- names and owners:
  - platform-api (owner: eng-platform/team-api) - REST control plane for routing and feature flags.
  - routing-svc (owner: eng-serving-runtime) - request routing, model variant fallback and cost-based policies.
  - batching-proxy (owner: eng-serving-runtime) - continuous batching and KV cache management.
  - telemetry-collector (owner: eng-platform/observability) - metrics, traces, and event enrichment.
  - infra-controlplane (owner: eng-infra) - terraform state, cloud accounts, network automation.

Each service above has a service-level runbook (linked in Related pages) and a short owner-runbook in the team wiki. The service owners are accountable for on-call rotation and runbook maintenance.

Runbooks: on-call triage and mitigation (quick reference)

1) Incident detection and first-response (0-10 minutes)
   - Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert within 2 minutes.
   - Post a short incident summary to #incidents (Slack) with the title: [PSS P1] <service> - <short symptom>.
   - Triage: determine if the issue is a single-service failure, cross-service degradation, or infra (network/cloud) problem.

2) Containment (10-25 minutes)
   - If the issue is request spikes or queue backlog: scale routing-svc and batching-proxy pools (see scaling commands below).
   - For partial degradations, enable automatic fallback policies: route affected customer tiers to compatible model-variants (policy id: fallback-compat-v2).
   - If telemetry is degraded, switch to retrospective logging mode: increase log-level to debug on telemetry-collector and enable supporting syslog export.

3) Recovery and postmortem (25+ minutes)
   - Restore healthy state and validate: run the smoke test suite (platform/smoketests/run) and confirm SLOs in Grafana.
   - Open a postmortem doc for any P1 or sustained P2 (>4 hours). Assign action items with owners and target dates.

Useful commands (CLI examples)

- Scale routing pool:
  - kubectl -n platform scale deployment routing-svc --replicas=10
- Restart batching-proxy pods gracefully:
  - kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/batching-proxy
- Check queue backlog (Kinesis example):
  - aws kinesis describe-stream --stream-name platform-requests | jq '.StreamDescription.Shards[] | {ShardId,SequenceNumberRange}'

Dashboards and alerting standards

- Single Grafana workspace: panels must use templated variables for cluster/env (prod/staging).
- Dashboards: each service must publish the following dashboards: Overview, Errors, Latency Heatmap, Capacity & Scaling.
- Naming convention: team.service.metric-dashboard (e.g., eng-serving-runtime.routing-svc-overview).
- Alert lifecycle: every alert must reference a runbook link and an expected suppression policy.

Key SLOs and alert thresholds

- Availability SLO (per-service): 99.9% monthly. Alert: paged when 10-minute rolling availability < 99.5%.
- Latency SLO: median p50 < 50ms, p95 < 300ms for control-plane APIs. Alert: paged when p95 > 800ms for 5 minutes.
- Error budget burn rate: page when 6-hour burn rate > 3x target.

Sample Prometheus alert rule (example)

- name: PSS-critical-rules
  rules:
  - alert: RoutingServiceHighLatency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="routing-svc"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.8
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "routing-svc p95 latency > 800ms"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/routing-svc-runbook"

Runbook ownership and maintenance

- Owners must review runbooks quarterly. Each runbook should include: quick mitigation steps, rollback commands, dashboards, relevant log queries, and postmortem links.
- Suggested review cadence: owner updates a runbook within 7 days after an incident if action items touch the runbook.

Retrospective: P1 outage on 2026-01-27 (summary)

- Incident summary: routing-svc experienced a memory leak in the request router causing progressive OOMs across 3 AZs. Automatic scaling delayed due to a misconfigured HPA threshold and a stale autoscaling policy in the control plane.
- Impact: 18 minutes full-service outage for 6% of traffic; elevated latency for 42 minutes.
- Root cause: two contributing issues: (1) a regression in the router's in-memory cache that increased retention, (2) HPA configured with a CPU-based threshold that under-reacted to queue length.
- Action items (status):
  - Fix: deploy memory leak patch (done 2026-01-29) - owner: eng-serving-runtime - status: completed.
  - Update HPA policy to use custom metrics (queue-length) for scaling routing-svc - owner: eng-infra - status: in_progress (ETA 2026-03-01).
  - Add p95 memory and queue-length alerts; reduce auto-scaling cooldown - owner: eng-platform/observability - status: completed.

Roadmap (prioritized, Q2-Q4 2026)

- Q2 2026 (high priority)
  - Consolidate Grafana workspaces and retire duplicate dashboards (owner: eng-platform) - success metric: <= 10 duplicate dashboards.
  - Migrate existing static Prometheus rules to templated rule-sets with runbook links (owner: eng-platform/observability).
  - Implement queue-length-based autoscaling for routing-svc and batching-proxy (owner: eng-infra).

- Q3 2026
  - Launch automated runbook verification tests that exercise playbook steps in a staging cluster (owner: eng-platform).
  - Introduce an alert de-duplication layer in the alertmanager pipeline to reduce noisy pages during deploys.

- Q4 2026
  - Platform catalogue: a lightweight UI in Console to surface service ownership, runbooks, and SLO status (owner: product).

How-tos (short procedures)

- Add a new dashboard:
  1. Create a new dashboard in the Grafana workspace using the team.service.metric-dashboard naming convention.
  2. Add templated variables for org, env, and cluster.
  3. Add a top-level panel that links to the runbook.
  4. Submit a PR to infra-dashboards repo with JSON export and request a review from eng-platform/observability.

- Update an alert rule:
  1. Open the alert-rule in the prometheus-rules repo.
  2. Add a runbook annotation and a suppression window if the alert overlaps deployments.
  3. Run the local lint (make lint-alerts) and the unit-style checks.
  4. Merge and monitor for two deploy windows.

Team wiki & knowledge base

- The team wiki contains short owner pages for each service (owner contact, on-call roster, quick links to dashboards and runbooks). Use the template: Team Service Owner Page (link in related pages).
- New hires: run the Platform on-call walkthrough (duration: 90 minutes). The walkthrough is required for all platform on-call assignees in their first 30 days.

Operational metrics and reporting

- Monthly report: platform health digest emailed to eng leadership including top incidents, SLO compliance, number of alert fires, and duplicate alerts metric.
- Quarterly review: consolidate action items from runbook reviews and retros into a roadmap epics list.

Appendix: useful links and artifacts

- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/
- Grafana workspace: grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/pss
- Prometheus rules repo: git@repo:redwood/infra-monitoring/prometheus-rules
- PagerDuty escalation policy: PagerDuty -> Escalation policy: PSS-Core

Document maintenance

- This playbook is owned by eng-platform. Review cadence: quarterly. For immediate edits, submit a PR to the confluence-sources repo and tag reviewers listed at the top.

If you are reading this as an on-call engineer: ensure you have access to the Grafana workspace, PagerDuty, and the infra GitHub org before your first shift.
